newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends down as election woes fade.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends down as election woes fade.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed down 90 basis points at 19.75 percent on Monday.
Dealers said demand for paper rose after a smooth electoral process on Sunday allayed fears that had driven up secondary rates last week.
"The market welcomed the election results. I had been a little worried over what might happen, but demand was heavy today, especially this morning," a trader said.
Overnight rates reached as low as 17.76 percent in early trade on an early surge in demand.
Mexico held elections on Sunday for the lower chamber of Congress, one-quarter of the Senate, six state governors and, for the first time in modern history, Mexico City mayor.

Cuauhtemoc Cardenas, of the left-wing Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) had a 22-point lead in the historic Mexico City race with 82 percent of the vote counted. Preliminary results showed the conservative National Action Party had taken control of two states from the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI).
Early returns showed the PRI was on course to lose its overall majority in the lower house, but it was still the largest single party and may have retained at least two states.
Dealers said a strong peso also helped drive down secondary interest rates. Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts had earlier closed 2.2 centavos stronger at 7.9210/7.9250 per dollar.
Banco de Mexico drained 3.398 billion pesos from the market by assigning three direct Cetes sales and six repos.
Overnight rates on bank paper paralleled government rates and dropped 110 basis points to 19.60 percent.

Dealers said the unusual fact bank paper traded at a lower rate than government paper was due to an anomalous rise in government rates following central bank intervention. Liquidity of 148 million pesos was due to return to the system on Tuesday from prior central bank operations.
